questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to

be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which conclusion/s logically follow/s from the given

statements.

Statements:

All beaches are sand.

Some deserts are sand.

All mountains are rocky.

Conclusions:

(I) At least some beaches are desert.

(II) At least some sands are rocky.
questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7393634ae88f3c543d428c8394c219a0fc70cfc9b324edc491fe9e8837b93834.png] 

Conclusions:

I. At least some beaches are desert → Does not follow (As all beaches are sand and some deserts are sand. So it is possible but not definite.)

II. At least some sands are rocky → Does not follow (As all beaches are sand, some deserts are sand and all mountains are rocky. So it is possible but not definite.)

∴ Here, Neither conclusion (I) nor (II) follows.​

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".

questions.question:
Select the word pair that best represents a similar relationship to the one expressed in the pair of words given below.

(The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of

letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word)

Control : Domination
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic:** Synonyms relationship**.

Control : Domination → **Control** is synonymous with **Domination**.

Similarly,

Manipulation : Deceive → **Manipulation **is synonymous with Deceive.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Manipulation : Deceive".**

questions.question:
In this question, three statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusion(s) logically follows/follow from the statements.

Statements:

No medicine is a capsule.

Some capsules are tablets.

Some tablets are laptops.

Conclusions:

I. Some capsules are laptops.

II. All tablets can never be medicines.

options.text: Neither Conclusion I nor II follow.
Both Conclusions I and II follow.

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2498166f0674db86ebfa2d3de39c2849acedd8501563b589cee21016713c09f4.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some capsules are laptops → Does not follow (As some capsules are tablets and some tablets are laptops. So it is possible but not definite.)

II. All tablets can never be medicines → Follow (As no medicine is a capsule and some capsules are tablets. As no direct relation is given between medicine and tablets, therefore it is false.)

∴ Here, Only Conclusion II follows.​

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3".

questions.question:
How many triangles are there in the given figure?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5ba42db7f361f9fbf9670ee305e42ceaff835b27a413bc852eff13cf047d821c.png]
questions.solution:
The number of triangles in the given figure is shown below:

1) Total triangles = [Number of parts × (1 + Number of parts)] ÷ 2

= [2 × (1 + 2)] ÷ 2

= [2 × 3] ÷ 2

= 6 ÷ 2

= 3

As there are 2 same types of triangles, therefore total number of triangles will be (3 × 2) = 6 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e07a7caf553f170f4cc76c3f707202879c720bed8b606bc9d6961ded48d3ad52.png]

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/44576f71cdb8902d88190b98966d0312f0463a404e8b5b7791c9af313f1eaa3a.png] 

Thus, there are total (6 + 12) = 18 triangles.

Hence, "Option 4" is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the number that will come in the place of the question mark(?), if ‘+’ and ‘ – ‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are

interchanged

93 – 7 ÷ 65 × 13 + 34 = ?
questions.solution:
BODMAS Table: 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d50192f098c21078501d30eeafe1a8c64bc30dd9621c48caa8a39ffc60f68b64.png] 

Given equation: 93 - 7 ÷ 65 × 13 + 34 = ?

Now, if ‘+’ and ‘-‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged, then:

⇒ 93 + 7 × 65 ÷ 13 - 34 = ?

Following BODMAS rule:

⇒ 93 + 7 × __**65 ÷ 13**__ - 34 = ?

⇒ 93 + __**7 × 5**__ - 34 = ?

⇒ __**93 + 35**__ - 34 = ?

⇒ __**128 - 34**__ = ?

⇒ __**94**__.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2".

questions.question:
Three of the following numbers are alike in a certain way and one is different. Pick the odd one out.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g., 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is: (First Number × 8) × First Number = Second Number

Option 1) 11 – 882

__(11 × 8)__ × 11 = 882

__88 × 11__ = 882

968 ≠ 882 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Option 2) 3 – 72

__(3 × 8)__ × 3 = 72

__24 × 3__ = 72

72 = 72 (LHS = RHS)

Option 3) 4 – 128

__(4 × 8)__ × 4 = 128

__32 × 4__ = 128

128 = 128 (LHS = RHS)

Option 4) 7 – 392

__(7 × 8)__ × 7 = 392

__56 × 7__ = 392

392 = 392 (LHS = RHS)

Thus, out of all the options '11 – 882' is the odd one out.

Hence, "Option 1" is the correct answer.
